statement: Prove by induction that $\\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^{2}=\\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$ for all positive integers $n$.
solution: Base $n=1$: LHS $=1$, RHS $=1\\cdot2\\cdot3/6=1$. Assume true for $n$. Then $\\sum_{k=1}^{n+1}k^{2}=\\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}+(n+1)^{2}=\\frac{(n+1)[n(2n+1)+6(n+1)]}{6}=\\frac{(n+1)(2n^{2}+7n+6)}{6}=\\frac{(n+1)(n+2)(2n+3)}{6}$, which is the formula with $n+1$. Hence proved.
